chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Lending wealth supports the Zakat.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between lending money and paying Zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) metaphorically describes lending money as the 'fence' or 'boundary' of Zakat, indicating that the liquidity provided by loans enables individuals to meet their Zakat obligations when their wealth is tied up in assets or goods. This narration, recorded in Al-Kafi, underscores the interplay between credit markets and obligatory charity in Shia jurisprudence, highlighting how financial mechanisms support religious duties. It reflects the practical wisdom of the Ahl al-Bayt in integrating economic activity with spiritual obligations.
